extracted.intended_audience: cognitive neuroscience researchers and neuroimaging scientists studying humor comprehension
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, running, and interpreting an event-related fMRI experiment that measures serial neural changes during comprehension of four-frame comic manga (introduction → development → turn → punch line). Focus is on mapping cognitive stages of humor (incongruity detection/resolution) to brain activations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-stage model of humor comprehension (incongruity detection and resolution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor comprehension requires incongruity detection and the resolution of incongruity between the expectations built by the story line and the consequence described in the punch line (Suls' incongruity resolution theory). The process is framed as a problem-solving cognitive task in which perceivers transform nonsense into humorous sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use experimental contrasts and time-resolved measures to separate detection and resolution stages; relate detection to early temporal activations (e.g., MTG/MFG) and resolution to frontal/parietal regions (e.g., SFG, IPL) as per cited literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-frame manga serial stages (introduction, development, turn, punch line)
rubrics_metrics.description: The four-frame manga structure is defined as: first scene = introduction, second = development, third = turn, fourth = conclusion/punch line. The time course of humor comprehension should be examined across these serial frames.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present each frame separately and analyze frame-by-frame activation changes to track the progression of cognitive and affective processes leading to humor appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation before punch line as a determinant of humor appreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong expectation formed before the punch line increases humor comprehension and appreciation; easy-to-predict story development aids incongruity resolution and amusement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select or design stimuli that vary predictability/expectation to test its effect on neural and behavioral measures of humor; compare stimuli where development cues a clear expectation vs. those that add new unexpected information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus selection via preliminary ratings and explicit thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: 219 four-scene manga were pre-rated on a 7-point emotional scale; 48 manga were selected based on these ratings and divided into 24 funny (score range 4.40–5.38, mean=4.59) and 24 non-funny (score range 2.20–3.20, mean=2.50) items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an independent preliminary rating sample to categorize stimuli and report selection thresholds and descriptive stats; ensure stimuli for each condition meet the predefined rating ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral funniness rating procedure during fMRI
rubrics_metrics.description: After viewing the fourth frame, participants responded using a four-score rating scheme with 4 being most funny and 1 being least funny; this rating was presented for 3000 ms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an in-scanner rating task synchronized with stimulus timing to obtain trial-by-trial funniness judgments; choose rating scale and response window explicitly and report mean and SDs per condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed-order (Mix) control condition
rubrics_metrics.description: A Mix condition composed of the same frames in randomized order (mixed ordered manga) is used as a control to compare serial-ordered (Funny) manga and isolate effects of coherent narrative order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a condition that disrupts serial narrative to test whether observed activations depend on story coherence/temporal order; contrast Funny vs Mix for each frame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization by subtracting first-frame baseline for frame comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: For comparisons of the second, third and fourth frames, fMRI data were normalized by subtracting data from the first frame (Funny 2 - Funny 1, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the first frame as baseline when assessing serial changes; explicitly report subtraction contrasts and rationale to control for baseline visual/semantic processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: fMRI trial timing and rapid event-related design
rubrics_metrics.description: Each frame presented for 3000 ms with jittered inter-stimulus intervals (ISI) of 4500, 6000 or 7500 ms between frames. Inter-trial interval similarly jittered; one trial lasted ~43–50 s; whole experiment ~25 min with 3 min rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt precise frame durations and jittered ISIs to enable event-related deconvolution; report trial length, number of trials, rest periods and timing parameters in methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant inclusion, demographics, and exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants were healthy undergraduate and graduate students (experiment 1: N=16, 9M/7F, age 21–26; experiment 2: N=18, 14M/4F, age 20–30). One subject excluded for excessive no-response trials (30/48). All provided informed consent under approved protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sample size, sex distribution, age range/means, consent/IRB approval, payment, and explicit exclusion criteria (e.g., excessive non-responses, movement).

rubrics_metrics.name: fMRI acquisition parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional images acquired on 3.0-T scanner (MAGNETOM Trio) with gradient-echo EPI: TR=3000 ms, TE=30 ms, flip angle=80°, FOV=192×192 mm, voxel size=3×3×3 mm. T1 anatomical: TR=2250 ms, TE=3 ms, flip angle=9°, voxel size=1×1×1 mm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify scanner, sequence type, TR/TE/flip angle, FOV and voxel dimensions for both functional and anatomical scans to ensure reproducibility and interpretation of temporal/spatial resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprocessing and first-level modeling choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional images realigned (head movements <4.0 mm), normalized, spatially smoothed with 8 mm FWHM Gaussian, high-pass filtered (128 s). Events modeled with a gamma hemodynamic response function (HRF). AR(1) model used for serial correlations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report motion limits, smoothing kernel, filtering parameters, HRF model, and noise/serial correlation modeling; justify choices and report any excluded volumes (first six images excluded).

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-level statistical thresholds and correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical thresholding used voxel-level p<0.001 (uncorrected for multiple comparisons) and cluster-level threshold p<0.05 (FWE corrected for multiple comparisons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State voxel and cluster thresholds, correction method (FWE), and whether voxel-level thresholding was uncorrected; provide tables of peak coordinates, BA, T-values and cluster sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Region-of-interest (ROI) creation and time-course analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: ROIs created using contrast images showing greater activation (p<0.001) between 4th frames of funny and non-funny manga. Percent signal changes extracted with MarsBaR; ROI sphere radius 5 mm; signal normalized to first time-point baseline; time-course analyzed with two-way repeated ANOVA (time-point × funniness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define ROI selection criteria (contrast and threshold), sphere size, baseline normalization, and statistical test for time-course (including corrections for multiple comparisons like Bonferroni).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specific software and analysis toolchain
rubrics_metrics.description: Data analyzed with SPM5 on MATLAB 7.3; MarsBaR used for ROI extraction; STATISTICA for ANOVAs. Reporting included MNI coordinates, BA labels, T-values and voxel counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List software versions and toolboxes used; provide details for reproducibility (e.g., scripts, parameters) and report coordinates in a standard space (MNI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral-statistical reporting conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavioral differences reported with means, SDs, t-tests and p-values (e.g., funniness ratings: Funny mean=2.99 SD=0.37 vs Mix mean=1.05 SD=0.09, t(14)=439.20, p<0.001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report full descriptive statistics (means, SDs), test statistics (t, F), degrees of freedom, and p-values; ensure consistency between behavioral and imaging contrasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting activation patterns in terms of cognitive/affective components
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign functional interpretations to region activations: TPJ implicated in early stages/incongruity resolution and mentalizing; STS/TP in mentalizing; MPFC in punch line understanding and affective appreciation; cerebellum and brainstem associated with amusement/laughter and reward-related processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground neural interpretations in prior literature and consider alternative explanations (e.g., working memory/semantic selection for IFG activation); corroborate imaging results with behavioral measures.
